entry.title: Authorization Bypass in Amazon Quick: Unauthorized AI Chat Agent Usage
entry.content:
Authorization Bypass in Amazon Quick: Unauthorized AI Chat Agent Usage
May 12, 2026

We discovered an authorization bypass in Amazon Quick’s AI Chat Agents that allows users to access and interact with AI agents despite explicit administrative restrictions. AWS responded by deploying a fix without notifying customers, classified the issue as “none,” and did not publish an advisory.

A technical analysis of a new AWS change to disabling SSE-C encryption. Read more about how we interpret AWS's design decisions and how we can improve our security by to protect against unique S3 ransomware.

State of Bug Bounties with AI: Analysis of curl and other Programs

Review of AI impact on bug bounty programs in 2026 including triage impact, report volume impact, and more. Analysis done on curl and other HackerOne programs.

entry.content:
Mistrusted Advisor: Evading Detection with Public S3 Buckets and Potential Data Exfiltration in AWS
August 20, 2025

We found security issues with AWS's Trusted Advisor Service that allowed us to create public S3 buckets while evading detection for potential data exfiltration.

entry.title: Introducing aws-size: A New Open Source Tool for Difficult Service Limit Visibility in AWS
entry.content:
Introducing aws-size: A New Open Source Tool for Difficult Service Limit Visibility in AWS
August 5, 2025

Releasing aws-size, a new open source tool to help with managing difficult service limits such as IAM policy size, bucket policy size, SCPs, RCPs, EC2 user data, and more. These limits may not be covered by AWS services such as Service Quotas or Trusted Advisor.

entry.content:
IAM SAR-ry: Deep Dive and Nuances of AWS's Programmatic IAM Action List and Service Authorization References (SAR)
July 15, 2025

AWS released a programmatic service reference for IAM. We did research and pulled statistics such as number of IAM actions, inconsistencies with the service authorization pages, access levels, changes in permission classification, and how this impacts your cloud security and IAM workflows.

entry.title: Hey ARNold: A Guide to All the Amazon Resource Identifiers Formats in AWS
entry.content:
Hey ARNold: A Guide to All the Amazon Resource Identifiers Formats in AWS
June 9, 2025

Securing AWS is hard. We programmatically pulled all of the amazon resource identifiers from AWS's documentation and compared it to other listings, even determining less than 21% resource coverage from AWS's own IAM policy generator.

entry.title: Shifty Business: Encryption in Amazon Redshift, Secure Defaults, and How to Shiftily Create Unencrypted Redshift Clusters
entry.content:
Shifty Business: Encryption in Amazon Redshift, Secure Defaults, and How to Shiftily Create Unencrypted Redshift Clusters
April 30, 2025

We uncovered inaccuracies in AWS documentation on data security and encryption for Amazon Redshift clusters. Redshift, a data warehousing database service, can have unencrypted resources configured via an encryption workaround via cluster modification via CloudFormation, CLI, and API despite AWS parameter checks on cluster creation and secure by default behavior changes.

entry.title: The Complexity of Detecting Amazon S3 and KMS Ransomware
entry.content:
The Complexity of Detecting Amazon S3 and KMS Ransomware
April 7, 2025

Detecting ransomware in Amazon S3 and KMS is complex. Not all events are logged by default and available tools can miss events due to nuances in logging. This post covers 11 different indicators of different types of ransomware in AWS, how they show in logs, and if these are logged by default. We cover CloudTrail (both data and management events) and Server Access Logging and how we've updated our open source YES3 Scanner tool to scan for Server Access Logging.

entry.title: YES3 Scanner: An Open Source Tool to Scan S3 Buckets for Access Misconfigurations and Ransomware Prevention
entry.content:
YES3 Scanner: An Open Source Tool to Scan S3 Buckets for Access Misconfigurations and Ransomware Prevention
March 26, 2025

Announcing Fog Security's latest open source tool: YES3 Scanner. YES3 scans Amazon S3 buckets to help prevent AWS access issues and check for security configurations including ransomware prevention. This includes checking for backups, account configuration, public access, and other S3 configuration items to help secure data in S3.

entry.title: The 18 Different Tagging Permissions for Amazon S3
entry.content:
The 18 Different Tagging Permissions for Amazon S3
February 9, 2025

A deep-dive into tagging on Amazon S3 and the 18 different IAM permissions to manage tags on S3 resources. This covers the inconsistencies in tagging, complexity of tagging in cloud, how it compares to other AWS services, and example policies.

entry.title: The Complete Guide to Cloud-Native Ransomware Protection in Amazon S3 and KMS
entry.content:
The Complete Guide to Cloud-Native Ransomware Protection in Amazon S3 and KMS
February 3, 2025

Fog Security's research on 11 different ransomware prevention use cases with AWS S3 and KMS. We utilize cloud-native settings including encryption via KMS, organizational policies such as service control policies and resource control policies, bucket policies, and account and bucket settings such as block public access. This post covers policy samples, code samples, and more to help with your ransomware protection.

entry.title: Ransomware in Amazon S3: SSE-C
entry.content:
Ransomware in Amazon S3: SSE-C
January 19, 2025

There's been an increase in recent ransomware via AWS SSE-C with customer-provided encryption keys. This research covers technical details, how to prevent against ransomware, and offers insight on reports from both AWS and Halcyon.

entry.title: Understanding RCPs and SCPs in AWS: Choosing the Right Policy for your Security Needs
entry.content:
Understanding RCPs and SCPs in AWS: Choosing the Right Policy for your Security Needs
January 15, 2025

Using both AWS Service Control Policies and Resource Control Policies can improve security and data perimeters within your cloud infrastructure. AWS recently released RCPs in late 2024, and this post covers how to leverage them together, nuanced reasons for adopting RCPs and SCPs, how to migrate to RCPs, code examples, and nuances and limitations of policy syntax for both.

entry.title: Securing Your Cloud Data: Unencrypted Resources in AWS
entry.content:
Securing Your Cloud Data: Unencrypted Resources in AWS
December 17, 2024

We look at what data can be unencrypted in Amazon Web Services, specifically which cloud services have resources that can be unencrypted. While most services offer encryption by default, certain resources can be unencrypted by default or also offer unencrypted options. This post covers observations, those AWS services, and recommendations to improve data security.

entry.title: Introducing Finders Keypers: A Open Source Tool to Discover Usage and Blast Radius of Encryption Keys in AWS
entry.content:
Introducing Finders Keypers: A Open Source Tool to Discover Usage and Blast Radius of Encryption Keys in AWS
November 29, 2024

Introduction of a new open-source tool, Finders Keypers that helps determine usage of KMS encryption keys to encrypt resources in Amazon Web Services (AWS). This tool helps with data perimeters, security and audit, determining blast radius, and helping understand usage and relationships of KMS keys.

entry.title: Creating a Data Perimeter with Resource Control Policies (RCPs) and AWS KMS
entry.content:
Creating a Data Perimeter with Resource Control Policies (RCPs) and AWS KMS
November 19, 2024

AWS recently released resource control policies as a new type of Organizational policies. These policies can control maximum permissions to resources within an organization. We look at the security impact and how to use these RCPs to craft data perimeters as well as when to use them compared to service control policies.

entry.title: Protecting Data and Preventing Ransomware: The IAM Guide to Managing and Updating Encryption for AWS Resources
entry.content:
Protecting Data and Preventing Ransomware: The IAM Guide to Managing and Updating Encryption for AWS Resources
October 21, 2024

A guide to IAM actions, nuances, and categorization of how to manage and update encryption for AWS resources with KMS. This helps with encryption management such as encryption key rotation, updating, and preventing against cloud data ransomware attacks where data is held hostage by removing access to encryption keys.

entry.title: The Complexity of AWS Data Access with KMS Encryption: KMS Key Grants and all the possible combinations
entry.content:
The Complexity of AWS Data Access with KMS Encryption: KMS Key Grants and all the possible combinations
September 12, 2024

Access to KMS and data access in Amazon Web Services can be complex. We look at a potential hidden access source and all the combinations of access that can be granted via KMS Key Grants. We take a different approach to look at evaluation with resource-based policies, IAM, and KMS Key Grants to see effective privilege and best practices for least privilege, encryption management, and data access

entry.title: Are my AWS Resources Encrypted or Unencrypted by Default?
entry.content:
Are my AWS Resources Encrypted or Unencrypted by Default?
July 16, 2024

This research focuses on an aspect of security by default by looking at AWS Resources and their encryption state by default when created. We look into encryption types including AWS Owned and AWS Managed default encryption by KMS, history of encryption by default settings, and additional settings and guardrails to help with cloud data security.

Deep Dive on AWS Support for AWS Managed Keys. We found 39 AWS Services that Support AWS Managed Keys and created documentation around service support, details and interesting details about AWS Managed Keys and their key policies, and created a tool to help you check support and access for AWS Managed Keys.

A look at Amazon Web Services's Block Public Access feature across AWS services such as EC2, S3, EMR, DynamoDB and how secure by default principles apply to account configuration to add additional layers of security as well as best practices for configuration.

A scenario with Amazon S3 where S3's Block Public Access Check can be circumvented to make a S3 Bucket public.

entry.content:

February 22, 2024

Research on AWS's Quantum Ledger Database and the misleading reporting of at-rest data encryption. Misleading reporting from encryption status may result in false positives for security and compliance of the QLDB and cause issues for security and application teams.
